budget_rule: three spec candidates per view, counting every --check run on a distinct spec; probes of the abandoned single-view shape are listed under abandoned_shapes

views.carries: wired uplink, wifi backup, gateway identity/qualifier

attempts.note: bond0 carried the LAN /24 text and e10 read 'metric 600, not ECMP'; extent 82 columns is over the 77 target, so the right-hand wifi label left the canvas.
shorter bond0 label and e10 'metric route'; extent 79 still over target, and a pinned COLUMNS=77 LINES=47 dump of THESE bytes showed 'graph overflows · drag to pan' on row 1 of the frame.

short node labels (bond0/wlp carry identity only) free the horizontal room that the edge labels need; the pinned 77x47 dump of the final bytes draws all four nodes and all four labels with no overflow banner. See evidence/v1/v1-lan-77x47-frames.txt.

views.carries: gateway -> ONT -> Verizon aggregation -> backbone -> Cloudflare, with NAT/pool, latency and v6 limits

attempts.note: the identity-map pattern's deep lr chain: five address-labelled ranks need 233 columns (3x the target) because every lr rank gap costs the label width + 3. This is the measured evidence for the tb deviation.

tb, four labelled hops, every edge label in a reserved gutter (label_slot). Clean check, but the gateway label still omitted the MAC-vendor evidence (WNC OUI) that the round-10 judge asked for, so the label was changed in place to the same width.

gateway label now reads 'Fios router 192.168.1.1 (hist., WNC OUI): ToR/spine/border/FW' (61 chars, the same box width as v1's label, so the layout is unchanged). Extent 63x36, no crossings, 4/4 labels, 0 ambiguous owners; pinned 77x47 dump draws the whole chain with no overflow banner.

views.carries: libvirt NAT bridge + VM, docker bridge + container, tailscale overlay and its UDP encap onto the wired NIC

attempts.note: no minlen: the engine ranked bond0 beside docker0/virbr0, making the middle rank three boxes wide. A pinned dump at COLUMNS=77 LINES=47 showed 'graph overflows · drag to pan' and clipped the rightmost label ('192.168.122.'). The a1 spec bytes are preserved as the recorded stdout of that probe; the file was overwritten by a2.

minlen 3 on ts -> bond0 reserves the corridor the source describes (the overlay is encapsulated over UDP on the wired path), so bond0 gets its own bottom rank and the middle rank drops to two boxes. Extent 72x32, 6/6 labels, 0 ambiguous owners, 0 crossings; pinned 77x47 dump clean. Shipped as specs/v3-virt-overlay.json (byte-identical copy of the a2 file).

abandoned_shapes.label: v1-lr-probe
abandoned_shapes.shape: one merged 8-node view of the whole egress chain (box, bond0, wlp, router, ONT, aggregation, backbone, Cloudflare) in lr
abandoned_shapes.why_abandoned: 372 columns cannot fit 77 at natural zoom; lr charges every hop the label's width plus 3.

abandoned_shapes.label: v1-tb
abandoned_shapes.record: attempts-log.jsonl labels v1-tb (one exit-127 record from an unset $BIN variable and its immediate re-run, both preserved verbatim)
abandoned_shapes.shape: the same merged 8-node view in tb, without label_slot
abandoned_shapes.why_abandoned: tb makes every labelled single-rank gap as tall as the label is wide (label width + 3 rows); seven ranks with eight labels cannot fit 46 drawing rows. Keeping the merged shape would have meant deleting labels, so the case split into the three views instead. label_slot (a one-row gutter) is the lever that made labels affordable in tb.

notes: No spec was checked twice under two labels; each --check in attempts-log.jsonl is a distinct spec except the v1-tb pair, where the first line is a shell-variable mistake and the second is the same spec run correctly.
The three final specs were also checked inside the evidence bundles (evidence/*/check.txt), so each shipped spec has two independent --check captures with identical lines.
